rated_messages.input_message: If this situation becomes stressful for you, make an excuse to leave for a few minutes. If this doesn't help, it might be better to just leave early.

When smoking, it can feel like your hands are for holding a cigarette, your mouth is for smoking the cigarette, and your chest and lungs need to breathe in the smoke. Spend 3 minutes noticing how your hands feel, how your mouth feels, and how your chest feels. The more you practice noticing these things without smoking, the sooner your body will stop being a trigger for you.
If you miss doing something with your hands, try turning a coin or pen over and over with your fingers.

Add the phrase “I’m having the thought that…” in front of your unhelpful thoughts. For example, “I’m having the thought that I need a cigarette.” Your thoughts are not always true or helpful! They are just thoughts.
Practice staying in this location without smoking. Just notice your urge. Practicing this will weaken this trigger with time. Just think of it as practice.

Some people find it helpful to give a name to their urge. If you're experiencing regular urges, give that feeling a name ('Olga the urge'?), and tell it that you won't give in to it. It may make it easier to live with (e.g. "ok Olga, I need to be by myself now...").
Life can get you really stressed out, but turning to cigs isn't the answer. Call or text family and friends instead. Ask them to help you stay on track.
You don’t need to get rid of or change your thoughts about smoking—just let them pass by like a cloud in the sky.
Crumple a piece of paper into a ball and imagine it is your urge. Toss the "urge" into the garbage or against the wall. By doing this, you are letting go of your urges.
What inspires you most to quit smoking? Are you willing to let this urge pass without smoking for that reason?
